interactions.description: Concurrent use significantly increases risk of bleeding. Monitor INR closely and watch for signs of hemorrhage.
Combination can cause electrolyte imbalances. Monitor potassium levels regularly.
Furosemide may increase metformin plasma levels, raising risk of lactic acidosis. Monitor renal function.

todos: Schedule INR monitoring appointment within 2 weeks due to Warfarin + Aspirin interaction
Review potassium levels at next lab draw — Furosemide + Spironolactone combination requires monitoring
Counsel patient on consistent Warfarin dosing and dietary vitamin K intake
Assess adherence barriers — overall adherence at 62%, below 80% target
Confirm Omeprazole is still needed; consider deprescribing if GERD is well-controlled

interactions.description: CNS depression risk. Sertraline may increase lorazepam sedation. Monitor for excessive drowsiness, respiratory depression.
SSRIs combined with NSAIDs/aspirin increase risk of GI bleeding. Confirm gastroprotection (omeprazole) is adequate.
Additive anticholinergic effects. Monitor for dry mouth, urinary retention, and constipation.

todos: Review Lorazepam use frequency — benzodiazepines in elderly patients carry fall and cognitive impairment risks
Assess COPD control: confirm patient is using inhaler technique correctly for all 3 inhalers
Discuss SSRIs + aspirin GI bleeding risk; confirm omeprazole is appropriate gastroprotection
Monitor blood glucose with metformin given reduced renal function risk in COPD patients
Schedule pulmonology follow-up if COPD exacerbations have increased

interactions.description: Anticholinesterase inhibitors and benzodiazepines have opposing mechanisms. Lorazepam may reduce donepezil efficacy and increase fall risk in elderly dementia patients.
Both cause CNS and respiratory depression. Combination significantly increases risk of sedation, falls, and aspiration pneumonia in elderly patients. Black box warning.
Calcium supplements can reduce alendronate absorption. Alendronate must be taken 30+ minutes before calcium or any food.

todos: URGENT: Review Quetiapine + Lorazepam combination — high-risk combination in elderly dementia patient
Evaluate alendronate administration timing — must be taken 30+ min before food and calcium supplements
Coordinate with caregiver to improve medication adherence; overall adherence 54%, significantly below target
Review quetiapine appropriateness — antipsychotics for BPSD carry FDA black box warning in elderly
Ensure vitamin D and calcium are adequately supporting bone health; check 25-OH vitamin D level

interactions.description: Carvedilol can increase digoxin levels. Monitor for digoxin toxicity signs: nausea, visual changes, bradycardia. Check digoxin levels periodically.
Furosemide-induced hypokalemia increases risk of digoxin toxicity. Ensure potassium levels remain in normal range.
ACE inhibitors can cause hyperkalemia. Combined with potassium supplementation, monitor serum potassium closely.

todos: Check digoxin serum level at next lab visit — interaction with carvedilol may elevate levels
Confirm potassium level is within therapeutic range given furosemide + digoxin combination
Review blood pressure log; patient may benefit from home monitoring given heart failure history
Assess for signs of ACE inhibitor cough from lisinopril; consider ARB switch if symptomatic

interactions.description: Combination increases seizure threshold lowering risk and serotonin syndrome risk. Monitor for agitation, tremors, or unusual behavior changes.
Two statins prescribed concurrently — unusual and may indicate duplication error. Review with prescriber to confirm clinical intent.
Biktarvy may slightly increase TMP-SMX levels. Monitor for sulfa-related adverse effects, though combination is generally well tolerated.

todos: REVIEW: Patient appears to be on two statins (Atorvastatin + Rosuvastatin) — confirm this is intentional with prescriber
Monitor for serotonin syndrome with Escitalopram + Bupropion combination
Confirm CD4 count and viral load at next lab; adjust TMP-SMX prophylaxis threshold if CD4 > 200
Screen for drug-drug interactions between Biktarvy and any new medications before prescribing

interactions.description: Phosphate binders like sevelamer can bind alendronate and reduce absorption. Alendronate should be taken separately (2+ hours) from sevelamer.
Sevelamer can bind iron and reduce absorption. Take ferrous sulfate at least 2 hours before or after sevelamer.
Both agents affect calcium/PTH balance. Combination requires close monitoring of calcium and PTH levels to avoid hypocalcemia.

todos: Review timing of sevelamer, alendronate, and ferrous sulfate to prevent drug binding interactions
Monitor PTH, calcium, and phosphorus levels — on both calcitriol and cinacalcet
Assess insulin dose adjustments based on renal function (ESKD reduces insulin clearance)
Confirm alendronate is appropriate for ESKD stage — bisphosphonates may be contraindicated at GFR < 30
Review anemia management: check hemoglobin, iron saturation, and darbepoetin response

interactions.description: NSAIDs can trigger aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) in asthma patients. Patient's allergy to NSAIDs is documented — Naproxen should be reviewed with prescriber immediately.
Additive effect for allergic rhinitis symptoms. Generally safe; minor sedation risk. Reassess if both are still required.

todos: URGENT: Patient has documented NSAID allergy but is prescribed Naproxen — contact prescriber immediately
Review NSAID sensitivity in asthma: consider acetaminophen as safer alternative for arthritis pain
Confirm asthma is well controlled; patient using rescue inhaler — track frequency of use
Counsel patient to continue excellent adherence; at 95%, this is a model patient

interactions.description: Both serotonergic agents. Risk of serotonin syndrome, seizures (lowered threshold with bupropion). Monitor for agitation, tremors, myoclonus.
Sertraline can increase zolpidem plasma levels. Monitor for excessive sedation, confusion, or next-day impairment.
Both agents lower blood glucose. Monitor for hypoglycemia, though risk is lower compared to insulin or sulfonylureas.

todos: Review Zolpidem use: benzodiazepine-related drugs in patients on SSRIs require regular reassessment
Assess depression response to Sertraline + Bupropion combination; consider psychiatric consultation
Check HbA1c to assess diabetes control; two agents (Metformin + Empagliflozin) should provide good coverage
Verify lithium allergy documentation — note in record that lithium cannot be used
Counsel on sleep hygiene as an alternative to ongoing Zolpidem use

interactions.description: Two mineralocorticoid antagonists prescribed simultaneously. Potential duplicate therapy — high risk of hyperkalemia. Confirm with cardiologist which agent is intended.
Patient has documented ACE inhibitor allergy. Sacubitril/Valsartan (an ARB) is appropriately used instead. Ensure no ACE inhibitors are ever prescribed.
Both are diuretics with complementary mechanisms. Monitor closely for volume depletion, hypotension, and electrolyte imbalances.

todos: URGENT: Review Spironolactone + Eplerenone duplicate therapy — high hyperkalemia risk; confirm with cardiologist
Monitor potassium levels closely given multiple agents affecting serum K+
Educate patient on fluid restriction and daily weight monitoring for heart failure self-management
Check renal function before adjusting dapagliflozin — contraindicated if eGFR < 25 for HF indication
Reassess metformin dose with insulin — risk of lactic acidosis in heart failure patients should be evaluated

interactions.description: Chronic corticosteroids combined with SSRIs increase risk of GI bleeding. Confirm adequate gastroprotection (PPI) is in place.
Sedative-hypnotics like Zolpidem can suppress respiratory drive, which is dangerous in COPD patients. Consider sleep hygiene interventions or lower-risk alternatives.
Combination of COX-2 inhibitor and corticosteroid increases GI ulcer and cardiovascular risk. Monitor for symptoms and consider PPI prophylaxis.

todos: Add PPI prophylaxis — patient on Prednisone + Celecoxib combination without gastroprotection noted
Evaluate Zolpidem use in COPD — respiratory depression risk; discuss with pulmonologist
Assess COPD exacerbation frequency; consider pulmonary rehabilitation referral
Review need for chronic oral prednisone — high long-term risk (osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression)
Counsel on smoking cessation if applicable — single most effective intervention for COPD progression
